units.title: Ancient India I — Stone Age to the Mahajanapadas, Jainism & Buddhism
units.why: The story of India opens here. Read it as one sweep — from the first tools through the Harappan cities, the Vedic age, the sixteen mahajanapadas and the rise of Magadha, into the new religions of Jainism and Buddhism — so each chapter clearly follows the one before it.

units.title: Polity I — The Constitution: making, features, rights & duties
units.why: Start Polity at its foundation: how the Constitution was made and evolved, its salient features and Preamble, then the Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles and Fundamental Duties that form the rights–duties core every later topic refers back to.

units.title: Economy I — Concepts, national income, planning & development
units.why: Build the economic vocabulary first: the basic features of the Indian economy, how national income is measured, the history of planning and NITI Aayog, and how poverty, unemployment and human development are tracked against it.

units.title: Ancient India II — Alexander, the Mauryas & the Deccan to Sangam
units.why: Pick the chronology straight back up: Alexander's invasion and the Indo-Greeks, the Mauryan empire and its successors, the Deccan Satavahanas (with the AP Satavahanas–Ikshvakus), the north-western Shakas and Kushanas, and the far-southern Sangam age.

units.title: Geography — physical to human (India & Andhra Pradesh)
units.why: Geography reads best as one connected run: the Earth and its landforms, atmosphere and oceans, then physical India and Andhra Pradesh, and finally the social and economic geography that sits on that physical base.

units.title: Polity II — Government, judiciary, federal structure & local bodies
units.why: With rights in place, study how the state is actually run: the Union and State executive and legislature, the judiciary, amendments and the basic-structure doctrine, Centre–State relations, the constitutional and statutory bodies, and local self-government.

units.title: Ancient India III — The Guptas, Harsha & post-Gupta kingdoms
units.why: Close the ancient era: the classical Gupta age, Harsha, and the post-Gupta regional kingdoms, consolidated with the key books, authors and foreign travellers that span the whole period.

units.title: Science & Technology — basics to space, biotech, health & environment
units.why: Science is applied in this exam, so learn it as one block: the core science basics and S&T policy, Indian scientists and institutions, then energy, space and defence, ICT, biotech and genetics, health and diseases, and environment and climate.

units.title: Medieval India — South Indian & Deccan kingdoms, Sultanate to Mughals
units.why: The medieval centuries belong together: the south Indian dynasties and the AP Kakatiyas, the tripartite struggle and the Delhi Sultanate, Vijayanagara–Bahmani with the AP Reddi and Qutb Shahi kingdoms, the Mughal empire, and the Bhakti–Sufi movements that run across them.

units.title: Economy II — Sectors, banking, fiscal policy, trade & the AP economy
units.why: The applied half of Economy: agriculture, industry and rural–urban development; money, banking and markets; fiscal policy, the budget and GST; the 1991 reforms, trade and WTO; environmental economics; and the Andhra Pradesh economy with the Reorganisation Act.

units.title: Modern India I — European companies, Company rule, 1857 & reform
units.why: Modern India begins with the Europeans: the trading companies, the governors and viceroys of Company and Crown rule, the Revolt of 1857, and the 19th-century socio-religious reform movements that followed.

units.title: Polity III — Governance, rights issues, IR & policies
units.why: Finish Polity with its applied themes: governance and e-governance, social-justice rights issues, the impact of LPG, India's foreign policy and international institutions, and major government policies and programmes.

units.title: Modern India II — The freedom struggle to Independence & integration
units.why: The climax of modern history as one connected narrative: the organised freedom movement and the Gandhian phase, Andhra's freedom struggle, Patel, Bose and Ambedkar, Independence and the integration of the princely states, and the formation of Andhra Pradesh.

units.title: Art & Culture — architecture, literature, science & AP culture
units.why: A compact capstone on culture: temple and Indo-Islamic architecture, classical and medieval literature and science, and Andhra Pradesh's own cultural heritage — building on the dynasties already studied.
